title: The Midnight Hollow
premise: Rosalind Quintana has survived twelve years in the city of Vell by hiding her beast-speaker gift behind a shop of harmless charms, but when the crown's witch-hunters burn the market and mark her for arrest, she flees with a smuggler's caravan into the Midnight Hollow — the borderland of a country erased from every map. There she discovers the erased nation, Ostrava, survives in a pocket between moonbeams, sustained by a door that only opens to a speaker's voice, and that the crown hunts her because her grandmother was the door's last keeper. Hunted by witch-finders and betrayed by the smuggler who loves her, Rosalind must choose between sealing herself safely inside Ostrava forever or speaking the truth that reopens the door for every refugee like her. She chooses truth, sacrifices her own passage, and becomes the new keeper — belonging not to one country, but to everyone the world erased.
about_author: Sebastian Ishikawa is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping disappearing villages before turning to fiction. They write at night, they claim, because that is when the erased places are easiest to find.

chapters.title: Charms and Cinders
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the market city of Vell, Rosalind sells trinkets while quietly bargaining with rats and pigeons for gossip and coin. When crown heralds post the Edict of the Thirteenth Moon — a hunt for the gifted — a witch-finder's hound stares at her and whines in recognition. The market burns that night. Emotional beat: the terror of a hidden life cracking open.

chapters.title: The Caravan of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Fleeing the ashes, Rosalind buys passage with smuggler Dario Voss, whose caravan carries refugees toward the Hollow. She conceals her gift even as dying horses whisper to her on the road. A checkpoint forces her first public use of magic — calming a panicked mule — witnessed by Dario. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of silence, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Where Maps Go to Die
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Dario, secretly reporting to the crown to protect his imprisoned sister, leads the caravan into the Midnight Hollow. He watches Rosalind speak with crows and begins questioning what he owes his handlers. The Hollow's fog erases the road behind them. Emotional beat: loyalty strained between the person in front of him and the sister behind him.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The caravan stumbles into Ostrava, a moonlit nation erased from history, populated by the disappeared. Its dying queen recognizes Rosalind's surname: Quintana, the keepers' line. Rosalind learns the door between worlds opens on the thirteenth moon-turn — and that the crown's hunt is really a search for the key. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering you are the inheritance you fled.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Vanished Tongue
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The old keeper, Maren, trains Rosalind in the deep speech that commands the door, but Rosalind's gift falters — beasts hear her, but stone and moon do not. Refugees in Ostrava welcome her warmly, and for the first time she belongs somewhere. Yet Maren warns: a keeper who opens the door can never leave. Emotional beat: belonging offered at the price of freedom.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finder's Hound
chapters.summary: Witch-finder Serane Kolt's POV. Serane tracks the caravan with a hound that once belonged to Rosalind's grandmother and still answers to the Quintana name. Through Serane we learn the crown's chancellor erased Ostrava generations ago to bury a scandal, and the door's reopening would expose it. Emotional beat: the hunter revealed as another servant of a lie.

chapters.title: What Dario Carried
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. The crown's agents threaten Dario's sister's life unless he opens Ostrava's gate from within. He signals them, then, wracked with guilt, confesses everything to Rosalind — and to the caravan, who turn on him. Rosalind spares his life but casts him out. Emotional beat: truth as both wound and absolution.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Rises
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Witch-finders breach Ostrava's border as the moon completes its turn. Maren dies holding the gate, passing the keeper's burden to Rosalind mid-siege. Rosalind's voice finally reaches the stone — but she realizes she can save either the refugees' escape or the country itself, not both. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Door and the Voice
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. Rosalind speaks the whole erased history of Ostrava aloud — through the door, into Vell, into every ear in the crown's city — making erasure impossible, because a country everyone has heard of cannot be unmade. The door stands open; the hunt collapses as soldiers refuse to arrest witnesses. Dario returns to hold the line beside her. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth reconciled at last.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, coda. Ostrava is redrawn onto maps; refugees choose freely between worlds. Rosalind, bound as keeper, watches Dario's caravan depart and knows he will return each full moon. She speaks with the hound that once hunted her, now her companion. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — she lost one home and inherited a doorway to all of them.
